name: Mitsubishi Ki-57-II Topsy
blurb: A twin-engine Army transport prepared as a Hangar-only Leyte campaign asset, with working propellers, landing gear, cargo doors and primary control surfaces.
history: The Ki-57 was Mitsubishi's transport development of the Ki-21 bomber family. The later Ki-57-II used Ha-102 engines and was known to the Allies as Topsy; a civil derivative was designated MC-20-II. This original model is a campaign-library representation, not yet a flyable aircraft.

sources.title: Mitsubishi Type 1 Ha-31 Model 21 (Ha-102), Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
